title: One answer, many wordings
statement: When a part has one intended answer, its scoring guide accepts other wordings of that answer, not related ideas or a broader or narrower category.
example: One guide accepted three related but distinct concepts as the one answer.
detail: Three separate reviews of the AP generator's short-answer items failed scoring guides that accepted related but distinct concepts as one answer, both an event and a whole era, or a document in place of the movement asked for (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/docs/analysis/evaluation_audit.md`; `icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/benchmark_runs/analysis_iter2.md`; `icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/benchmark_runs/failures_20260226_172346.md`). The first review said the mixed list created grading inconsistency, and the second called it an internal contradiction. The rule is for a part with one intended answer; a part that asks for one example among many is a different case.
against: Parts that ask for one example out of many rightly accept several distinct answers, and official scoring guidelines list them ('Examples that earn this point include the following:', `icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/curriculum/ceds/ap-european-history-ced.pdf`). The generator's own writer rules push for inclusive lists of every valid response (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/generators/saq.py`).

evidence.quote: 4. The accepted answers (popular sovereignty, consent of governed, social contract) are related but distinct concepts, creating grading inconsistency
Part (a) scoring criteria lists both 'Compromise of 1877' and 'Reconstruction' as acceptable answers, which creates an internal contradiction
